independent_solution: Full stem read on the pinned pages 20-21: (a) |a+b| <= |a|+|b|, (b) |a+b| >= ||a|-|b||, (c) |a-b| <= |a|+|b|, (d) |a-b| >= ||a|-|b||; when does equality apply?

Draw a and b head to tail: a, b, a+b form a triangle, so the side |a+b| is at most the sum and at least the difference of the other two sides -> (a), (b). Replace b by -b (same magnitude): a, -b, a-b form a triangle -> (c), (d).
The triangle degenerates to a line only for collinear vectors: (a) and (d) become equalities when a, b are parallel (same direction); (b) and (c) when a, b are antiparallel (or either is zero).
questions.independent_answer: All four follow from the triangle inequality; equality holds only for collinear vectors ((a),(d) parallel; (b),(c) antiparallel).
questions.official_answer: Hint: the sum (difference) of any two sides of a triangle is never less (greater) than the third side. Equality holds for collinear vectors.

independent_solution: Full stem read on pinned page 21 including option (d). a+b+c+d = 0 closes a head-to-tail polygon; (a) is false: four non-zero vectors can close a quadrilateral.
(b) a+c = -(b+d), so |a+c| = |b+d|: true. (c) a = -(b+c+d), so |a| = |b+c+d| <= |b|+|c|+|d|: true.
(d) b+c = -(a+d); a+d lies in the plane of a and d (on their line if collinear), so b+c does too: true.
Rewrite each relation with one vector alone: (a) c = a+b, (b) a = b+c, (c) b = a+c, (d) a+b+c = 0 (closed triangle).

Read arrow directions on the pinned figure (page 6): (i) a up, c from head of a to the right, b from origin to that point -> b = a+c; (ii) a right, b up from head of a, c back to origin -> a+b+c = 0; (iii) c left from origin, b from tail of c up to the top, a from origin up -> a = c+b; (iv) a left, b down from head of a, c from origin to bottom-left -> c = a+b.
questions.official_answer: (a) matches with (iv), (b) matches with (iii), (c) matches with (i), (d) matches with (ii)
